sections.h2: Who do I call about a Wayne County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Monticello has all three desks. One office values the parcel, one collects the money, and one picks up the leftovers: PVA, Sheriff, and County Clerk, in that order through the year.

The PVA sits at 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107, Monticello, KY 42633, phone 606-348-6621. Beyond the usual weekday hours of 8 to 4, the county advertises Saturday service on the first and third Saturday of the month, 8 a.m. to noon. That is the easiest time for a working owner to ask about a value or an exemption. For a lost bill or a payment question, ask the Sheriff's Office in Monticello for its current phone and window hours.

The fiscal court, the school board, and special districts vote the rates. Valuation is the PVA's only role.

sections.h2: Which late charges apply to Wayne County tax?
sections.html:
Each month of delay costs money, on the schedule of KRS 134.015, and the Sheriff takes payment until April 15. A full payment made by November 1 saves 2 percent, and a payment made after January 31 costs 10 percent extra.

  • Up to November 1: the 2 percent discount.
  • Rest of November and December: the number printed on the bill.
  • During January: 5 percent more.
  • February 1 through April 15: a 10 percent surcharge.

Frankfort can swap in a calendar of 30-day blocks if its mailing runs late, so trust the dates on your own bill.

sections.h2: How does an owner contest a Wayne County value?
sections.html:
A conversation at the PVA's counter has to come first. State rules do not allow an appeal to be filed without it, and the staff must explain the valuation method and keep notes. Then the steps below apply.

Appeal steps for Wayne County property owners
StepWhen
Public inspection of the roll13 days beginning the first Monday in May
Talk with the PVAAnytime after notices go out, before filing
Written appeal at the County ClerkClose of business the day after inspection ends
Hearing before the local board25 to 35 days after inspection, up to five days of sessions

The board wants proof it can see: insurance policies, construction cost, listings, and the physical features of land and buildings. Owners near Lake Cumberland should document docks, decks, and outbuildings as they stood on January 1. Missing the hearing after filing cuts off a further appeal.

sections.h2: Can a senior in Wayne County pay less property tax?
sections.html:
Yes. The homestead exemption subtracts $49,100 from what is taxed on a person's own residence in 2025 and 2026. Qualifying means turning 65, or being declared totally disabled under a federal program or a retirement system.

With the Census median home value of $135,700, the deduction leaves $86,600 taxable. At Frankfort's 2025 levy of 10.6 cents on each $100, that trims the state's portion from about $143.84 to about $91.80. Local districts levy additional rates.

  • File the state's homestead and disability form at the Wayne County PVA.
  • Proof of age can be a passport, license, or birth certificate.
  • Disability payments must have been received through the whole assessment period.
  • A veteran's service-connected disability or a permanent total ruling by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems removes the yearly renewal.

sections.h2: Do unpaid Wayne County taxes block a sale?
sections.html:
Not by themselves, but they come out of your proceeds. Under KRS 134.420 the delinquency lien stays on the parcel for up to eleven years, and a buyer's title company will want it cleared.

Once at the Clerk the amount grows by a penalty, a Sheriff's add-on, and monthly interest. Commissions for the clerk and county attorney, mailing costs, and a lien recording fee follow. Revenue's illustration shows a $1,000 bill passing $1,600 within weeks.

Beyond that, an investor can buy the certificate at a sale and add charges. Paying the Sheriff before April 15 sidesteps the path, and the sales contract should spell out who covers this year's bill.

sections.h2: What is Wayne County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
On the Tennessee border, Wayne County was cut from Pulaski and Cumberland counties on December 13, 1800, and honors General Anthony Wayne. Monticello is the lone city and the seat. About 458 square miles of land reach into the Daniel Boone National Forest and meet Lake Cumberland, a reservoir the county's website credits with 1,255 miles of shoreline. Mill Springs was the scene of the January 19, 1862 battle that ended with the Confederate commander's death.

Time zones matter here. Wayne County keeps Eastern time, though its west and south edges trace the Central time line, so a lender or attorney across that line may be an hour apart. Public schools belong to Wayne County Schools, which absorbed Monticello Independent on June 30, 2013, and the Area Technology Center teaches welding, carpentry, health science, and other trades.

  • Population 19,597 in 2025, up 0.2 percent from 2020 but below the 20,813 of 2010.
  • 10,206 housing units against 8,074 households, a 2,132 unit difference.
  • Owners live in 69.1 percent of homes; the middle value is $135,700.
  • Half of households earn under $45,739, and 28.8 percent of people are below the poverty line.
  • Gross rent has a median of $727; 22.7 percent of residents are 65 or older.

The county is also known for folk music: fiddler Dick Burnett, who wrote "Man of Constant Sorrow," was born near Monticello. Owners with inherited cabins, rentals, or homes that need work can sell as-is for cash and settle taxes at the closing table.

Settlement here is old. Longhunters camped near Mill Springs on the Cumberland River in the 1770s, and a log cabin built in 1775 grew into Price's Station, one of the earliest settlements in Kentucky. The land was Cherokee homeland, and conflict followed as more settlers arrived. Revolutionary War veterans received grants in lieu of back pay, and several arrived between 1794 and 1799. During the winter of 1861 the Confederate government of Kentucky passed an act to rename the county Zollicoffer County.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about owning a house in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Monthly costs are modest. Census figures show median owner costs of $1,100 with a mortgage and $342 without, so a paid-off house in Wayne County is cheap to hold.

Labor force participation is 48.5 percent for people 16 and over. Among adults 25 and over, 80.9 percent finished high school and 13.9 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Health care and social assistance receipts of $57.9 million in 2022 trail retail sales of $234.6 million. The county has 284 employer establishments with 4,114 workers, and workers travel 24.8 minutes to work on average. The county counts 983 veterans, and 85.7 percent of households subscribe to broadband.

Landmarks show up in the listing story of older houses: the 1877 Mill Springs Mill still grinds, the Brown-Lanier House was Confederate headquarters before the 1862 battle, and the Raccoon John Smith Cabin and Doughboy Monument on the Monticello square draw visitors. The county voted wet on November 3, 2020, by 4,901 to 3,966. Elevation across the county runs from 656 to 1,870 feet.

The long-run population curve is worth a glance. Wayne County recorded 17,518 residents in 1910, fell to 14,268 by 1970, climbed to 19,923 in 2000, peaked at 20,813 in 2010, and counted 19,555 in 2020, a drop of 6.0 percent in the last full decade. The Monticello airport sits at 963 feet, and KY 90 marks part of the time zone line on the county's western side.

faqs.q: What are the Wayne County PVA's hours?
faqs.a: At 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107 in Monticello, the PVA opens weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus the first and third Saturday of the month 8 a.m. to noon. The phone is 606-348-6621.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Wayne County tax early?
faqs.a: Yes, 2 percent for paying the entire bill by November 1. The printed amount holds through December, then 5 percent and later 10 percent are added.

faqs.q: Must I talk to the Wayne County PVA before I can appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. You must confer with the PVA or a deputy first, and then file with the County Clerk by closing time on the day after inspection ends.

faqs.q: How big is the Wayne County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It deducts $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 from the value of the home you live in. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, file at the PVA.

faqs.q: Who gets my Wayne County tax bill after April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk takes it as a certificate of delinquency backed by a lien. Interest and commissions accumulate, and an investor can purchase it at a sale.
